limits.title: Policy source
limits.counting: Final SBPL source after augments; excludes terminating NUL. Imported file contents are not added to this count.
limits.effect: Excess rejects the specimen after decoding and before semantic validation or process work: bad_request with host-owned admission_failure.
limits.behavior: At-limit, over-limit and multibyte admission controls through the CLI.

limits.title: Probe steps
limits.counting: Entries in probe_plan.
limits.effect: Excess rejects the specimen after decoding and before semantic validation or process work: bad_request with host-owned admission_failure.
limits.behavior: At-limit, over-limit and multibyte admission controls through the CLI.

limits.title: Policy parameters

limits.effect: Excess rejects the specimen after decoding and before semantic validation or process work: bad_request with host-owned admission_failure.
limits.behavior: At-limit, over-limit and multibyte admission controls through the CLI.

limits.title: Step ID

limits.effect: Excess rejects the specimen after decoding and before semantic validation or process work: bad_request with host-owned admission_failure.
limits.behavior: At-limit, over-limit and multibyte admission controls through the CLI.

limits.effect: Excess rejects the specimen after decoding and before semantic validation or process work: bad_request with host-owned admission_failure.
limits.behavior: At-limit, over-limit and multibyte admission controls through the CLI.

limits.counting: Arguments supplied in attempt.args; the target occupies the additional argv[0] slot.
limits.effect: Excess rejects the specimen after decoding and before semantic validation or process work: bad_request with host-owned admission_failure.
limits.behavior: At-limit, over-limit and multibyte admission controls through the CLI.

limits.title: Each supplied exec argument
limits.counting: Each supplied argument, excluding terminating NUL; the target has its own larger limit.
limits.effect: Excess rejects the specimen after decoding and before semantic validation or process work: bad_request with host-owned admission_failure.
limits.behavior: At-limit, over-limit and multibyte admission controls through the CLI.

limits.title: Parameter key
limits.counting: Each key, excluding terminating NUL. A refused key is identified by field and byte count only, never echoed.
limits.effect: Excess rejects the specimen after decoding and before semantic validation or process work: bad_request with host-owned admission_failure.
limits.behavior: At-limit, over-limit and multibyte admission controls through the CLI.

limits.title: Parameter value
limits.counting: Each value, excluding terminating NUL.
limits.effect: Excess rejects the specimen after decoding and before semantic validation or process work: bad_request with host-owned admission_failure.
limits.behavior: At-limit, over-limit and multibyte admission controls through the CLI.

limits.title: Query operation
limits.counting: Each sandbox_check.operation, excluding terminating NUL. Host-only: the string goes to the validator line and is echoed per step in the reply; it never enters shared memory.
limits.effect: Excess rejects the specimen after decoding and before semantic validation or process work: bad_request with host-owned admission_failure.
limits.behavior: At-limit, over-limit and multibyte admission controls through the CLI; constructed orchestrator controls refuse before any process work and cover every filter kind.

limits.title: Query filter value
limits.counting: Each sandbox_check.filter.value when present, for every filter kind including none and unrecognized kinds, excluding terminating NUL. Independent of the attempt target: a step may query one path and attempt another, and each string is bounded on its own.
limits.effect: Excess rejects the specimen after decoding and before semantic validation or process work: bad_request with host-owned admission_failure.
limits.behavior: At-limit, over-limit and multibyte admission controls through the CLI; constructed orchestrator controls refuse before any process work and cover every filter kind.

limits.title: Probe filter and attempt labels
limits.counting: Each sandbox_check.filter.kind, attempt.kind and attempt.action, excluding terminating NUL. Unknown labels within the bound retain their per-step prediction_unavailable or unsupported behavior.
limits.effect: Excess rejects the specimen after decoding and before semantic validation or process work: bad_request with host-owned admission_failure.
limits.behavior: Exact, over-limit and multibyte boundaries through the CLI; 256-step oversized-label regressions require a small refusal and unchanged write targets.

limits.title: Specimen ID
limits.counting: The specimen_id string, excluding terminating NUL. Echoed once per reply; a refused ID is replaced by the placeholder <admission_refused>.
limits.effect: Excess rejects the specimen after decoding and before semantic validation or process work: bad_request with host-owned admission_failure.
limits.behavior: Exact, over-limit and multibyte boundaries through the CLI and in constructed controls; the refusal reply never contains the refused string.

limits.title: Request labels
limits.counting: Each of run_kind and policy.format, excluding terminating NUL. Echoed once per reply; a refused run_kind is omitted and a refused format reads unknown.
limits.effect: Excess rejects the specimen after decoding and before semantic validation or process work: bad_request with host-owned admission_failure.
limits.behavior: Exact, over-limit and multibyte boundaries through the CLI and in constructed controls; an at-limit format passes admission and fails as bad_policy.

limits.title: Test-seam executable paths
limits.counting: Each of _test_overrides.libsandbox_path, worker_executable_path and validator_executable_path, excluding terminating NUL. Mirrored back in test_overrides and named in dlopen and spawn diagnostics; every invalid path is independently dropped from a refusal mirror, even if another field is reported first.
limits.effect: Excess rejects the specimen after decoding and before semantic validation or process work: bad_request with host-owned admission_failure.
limits.behavior: Exact, over-limit and multibyte boundaries through the CLI and in constructed controls; at-limit nonexistent paths pass admission and reach their own seam failures.

limits.title: Worker readiness hint wait
limits.counting: Initial ready-byte polling budget.
limits.effect: Expiry alone does not abort: the host still checks shared-memory publication.
limits.control: Production default; test-only controls are not a public tuning interface.
limits.behavior: Normal readiness is tested; expiry without aborting is source-inspected.

limits.title: Worker publication wait
limits.counting: Nominal host polling budget from the end of the ready-byte wait until done. Synchronous validator work is outside this count; policy transfer before polling and scheduler delays are separate. The worker uses a separate local active-time budget for exec attempts.
limits.effect: Expiry can trigger worker cleanup and runner_timeout with partial evidence. The exec budget is configured below this window but does not guarantee an end-to-end deadline.
limits.control: Production default; test-only controls are not a public tuning interface.
limits.behavior: Deadline and partial-publication paths use shortened test budgets; the production duration is source-inspected.

limits.title: Worker exit grace
limits.counting: Polling grace after the host requests exit.
limits.effect: Expiry triggers a SIGKILL attempt, then reaping. Kill/reap failures remain reported.
limits.control: Production default; test-only controls are not a public tuning interface.
limits.behavior: Deadline/cleanup paths use controlled children; the production duration is source-inspected.

limits.title: Worker release wait
limits.counting: Elapsed CLOCK_MONOTONIC time after successful apply, before host release acknowledgement.
limits.effect: Expiry or clock failure publishes a proceed failure and done with no attempts. The existing exit-request spin can outlive a dead host.
limits.control: Production default and internal test equipment; not a public CLI tuning interface.
limits.behavior: Short-budget, delayed-release, clock-failure and delayed-cleanup controls establish fail-closed behavior; production duration is value-checked.

limits.title: Nominal release margin
limits.counting: Configuration allowance for host observation, setup, decoding and scheduling, not a separately enforced timer.
limits.effect: Production defaults satisfy 60000 > 30000 + 1000 + 5000. This guard does not cover test overrides or bound final blocking reap, host descheduling, prompt replies or eventual orphan cleanup.
limits.control: Production default and internal test equipment; not a public CLI tuning interface.
limits.behavior: Short-budget, delayed-release, clock-failure and delayed-cleanup controls establish fail-closed behavior; production duration is value-checked.

limits.title: Validator I/O test override floor
limits.counting: Minimum effective _test_overrides.validator_io_timeout_ms; request schema remains 1.
limits.effect: Changes only the real validator I/O deadline, with no ceiling. Over-budget values may intentionally outlast the worker release wait; expiry cannot revive attempts. The supplied value is mirrored in every reply.
limits.control: Production default and internal test equipment; not a public CLI tuning interface.
limits.behavior: Short-budget, delayed-release, clock-failure and delayed-cleanup controls establish fail-closed behavior; production duration is value-checked.

limits.title: Validator I/O deadline
limits.counting: Elapsed CLOCK_MONOTONIC deadline for nonblocking probe writes and verdict reads; wall-clock changes cannot extend it.
limits.effect: Retains received verdicts and records an I/O timeout; cleanup follows.
limits.control: Production default; _test_overrides.validator_io_timeout_ms replaces this deadline, floored at 50 ms without a ceiling and mirrored in results.
limits.behavior: I/O deadline and partial-evidence paths use shortened budgets; the production duration is source-inspected.

limits.title: Validator exit grace
limits.counting: Polling grace after closing validator pipes.
limits.effect: Expiry triggers a SIGKILL attempt, then reaping; failures remain reported.
limits.control: Production default; test-only controls are not a public tuning interface.
limits.behavior: Cleanup paths use controlled children; the production duration is source-inspected.

limits.title: Exec child deadline
limits.counting: Child observation time after successful spawn, limited by the earlier of its absolute deadline and the local exec plan deadline. Time spent spawning cannot restart the plan budget.
limits.effect: EOF and child exit are observed separately. Deadline or observation failure requests process-group termination while the leader is still owned, even if that leader already exited. A deadline makes the attempt fail while preserving any observed natural exit code. A successful leader reap does not prove every descendant stopped.
limits.control: Production default; test-only controls are not a public tuning interface.
limits.behavior: Live controls close streams while both processes remain alive and exit the leader while a descendant retains streams. Independent socket credentials, OS exit events and file effects establish the behavior.

limits.title: Exec attempt budget
limits.counting: Local CLOCK_MONOTONIC active time starting before worker setup. Only the interval returned by the release barrier is excluded. An absolute cutoff is passed to exec attempts; this is not a reconstruction of the host polling clock.
limits.effect: An exhausted budget refuses spawn with exec_failed and ETIMEDOUT, no child identity and no sandbox attribution. Clock failure before spawn refuses the attempt; clock failure after spawn triggers cleanup and is retained as an observation error. Blocking spawn and non-exec operations are not preemptible here.
limits.control: Production default leaves a nominal 5,000 ms margin below worker_sentinel_wait. Internal test equipment may shorten it independently; the specimen worker_timeout_ms override does not move it.
limits.behavior: Compiled values agree with the host configuration. Deterministic native controls vary spawn latency, release exclusion, intervening work, exact exhaustion, clock failures and cleanup. Real short-budget plans preserve completed prefix and trailing file effects through host assembly and serialization.

limits.title: Exec child reap grace
limits.counting: Local monotonic observation window for nonblocking waitpid after exec observation stops.
limits.effect: Expiry, clock failure or native wait failure retains an unconfirmed reap without inventing exit status. Failed group termination permits only an immediate nonblocking reap. This does not bound a native syscall or host descheduling.
limits.behavior: Controlled pending/EINTR waits exhaust the grace; kill, wait and clock failures retain missing status. Every wait is required to be nonblocking.

limits.title: Exec attempt descriptors
limits.counting: Descriptors opened before sandbox application per exec step: both ends of stdout and stderr pipes. Before opening any, the worker scans for free descriptor numbers, accounting for inherited descriptors, and raises its soft limit to fit the plan plus the descriptor reserve. Raises are capped at the hard limit and OPEN_MAX (10,240); an already higher soft limit is preserved.
limits.effect: Only exec slots that fit without spending the reserve get pipes. Excess slots report exec_failed with errno 24 and an exec descriptor budget diagnostic naming the limit; no pipe syscall or child spawn is claimed. Actual pipe failures report their own syscall and errno. Budget refusal is per-step evidence, with sandbox attribution unestablished; imports and other attempts retain descriptor headroom.
limits.control: Host-derived hard ceiling; no public override. The worker raises the soft limit and never lowers it.
limits.behavior: The per-step count is value-checked against the compiled worker. A 256-exec plan is pinned live through the CLI. Native harness cases cover a raised soft limit, 80 extra inherited descriptors, and hard caps 64 and 126 through 129 with policy imports and reads before/after execs. Every prepared child must exit cleanly and excess slots must report budget refusal. The OPEN_MAX clamp is source-inspected.

limits.title: Exec descriptor reserve
limits.counting: Free descriptor slots withheld from exec pipe setup, in addition to descriptors already open. The worker scans with fcntl(F_GETFD) to find room for this reserve plus four descriptors per exec step.
limits.effect: Preserves headroom for policy compilation/imports, file probes, and spawn file actions. If the inherited/hard limit already leaves fewer free slots than the reserve, exec setup opens no pipes. This bounds exec pipe consumption; it does not guarantee that arbitrary imports or other resource users fit.
limits.behavior: Value-checked against the compiled worker. Capped mixed plans require successful policy imports and file reads even when all exec slots are refused, and clean exits for every prepared exec. The inherited-descriptor case requires all 32 execs with ample hard-limit capacity.

limits.title: Runner RPC wait
limits.counting: Client wait for the runner reply.
limits.effect: An expired wait yields runner_timeout; it does not expand the inner worker or validator budgets.
limits.control: Default; --timeout-ms changes only this wait and floors its value at 1 ms.
limits.behavior: The production wait and timeout response are source-inspected; compiled default agreement is tested.

limits.title: Validator query payload
limits.counting: Serialized JSON bytes for one probe, before the LF delimiter. Escaping counts. The fixed 65536-byte buffer retains the 65534-byte payload allowance; the reader counts physical bytes, including raw NUL, and drains the rest of an overlong line.
limits.effect: An overlong line produces one parse_error with no step ID; that prediction is unavailable. Later lines can still be processed. Admitted specimens cannot reach it: with the operation and filter value admission-bounded, a fully escaped probe line stays a few KiB.
limits.behavior: Exact payload boundary, over-limit drain/recovery, valid raw and escaped Unicode, malformed escapes/UTF-8/raw controls and raw-NUL physical framing. Every rejected probe is followed by a valid recovery probe.

limits.title: Synthesized maximal reply
limits.counting: Encoded size, through the production encoder, of the field-complete reply fixture with 256 steps, 256 validator records and disposition entries, every request- or host-derived string at its documented limit and made of U+0001 (six JSON bytes per byte), the largest worker diagnostic, and the largest slash-heavy compiled-profile receipt. An upper bound for the current response schema: fields that cannot co-occur in one run are all present.
limits.effect: Not enforced anywhere; it derives the runner client budget. A reply string key added to the fixture without a size classification fails runner_unit, so the number cannot silently fall behind the schema.
limits.control: Recomputed by runner_unit; edit the manifest when the synthesizer's number moves.
limits.behavior: The synthesizer's value is compared with the manifest; the budget relation is asserted; an injected unclassified key is detected. Live 256-step workloads are measured against this bound.

limits.title: Runner client output
limits.counting: Per stdout or stderr stream captured from the runner client. Byte prefix before lossy text decoding; not an envelope-wide cap.
limits.effect: Output beyond the prefix is marked truncated. Truncated JSON stdout is not parsed as a complete reply.
limits.control: Derived: three times runner_reply_maximum, rounded up to a whole 4 MiB. runner_unit asserts the relation against the compiled Rust constant's documented value; no public override.
limits.behavior: Exact prefix and truncation-boundary controls, including small arbitrary budgets and every cut within multibyte scalars. Collection buffers the entire stream first; this is not a memory limit. Five admitted 256-step CLI workloads at the admitted maxima, including the control-character exec workload with 511-byte targets and queries, 63-byte step IDs, maximal metadata and live profile capture, must each stay under runner_reply_maximum; the budget then holds a complete reply with a threefold margin by construction.

limits.title: Log observer stdout
limits.counting: Raw observer stdout bytes, enforced while reading; includes the JSON report and final newline. Independent stderr has its own cap.
limits.effect: One extra byte witnesses overflow; retain only the bounded raw prefix without JSON fragment recovery and withhold correlation.
limits.control: Fixed. Sized for bounded inner text, duplicated deny lines and parsed raw lines, six-byte JSON escaping, event metadata and reply metadata.
limits.behavior: Streaming cap controls cover both pipes. A 256-record corpus preserves all records; exact inner stdout/stderr caps with maximum escaping fit the bounded serializer. Interrupted or failed capture changes log evidence only.

limits.title: Log show stdout
limits.counting: Raw bytes read from log show stdout, before decoding or parsing; enforced while reading.
limits.effect: One extra byte witnesses overflow; retain only the budgeted prefix, stop collection, clean up and withhold correlation.
limits.behavior: Both stream boundaries are tested at, below and above a substituted small cap, including concurrent stdout/stderr. Counts describe bytes actually read, never the unavailable remainder.

limits.title: Log show stderr
limits.counting: Raw bytes read from log show stderr, before decoding or parsing; enforced while reading.
limits.effect: One extra byte witnesses overflow; retain only the budgeted prefix, stop collection, clean up and withhold correlation.
limits.behavior: Both stream boundaries are tested at, below and above a substituted small cap, including concurrent stdout/stderr. Counts describe bytes actually read, never the unavailable remainder.

limits.title: Log observer stderr
limits.counting: Raw bytes read from observer stderr, before decoding or parsing; enforced while reading.
limits.effect: One extra byte witnesses overflow; retain only the budgeted prefix, stop collection, clean up and withhold correlation.
limits.behavior: Both stream boundaries are tested at, below and above a substituted small cap, including concurrent stdout/stderr. Counts describe bytes actually read, never the unavailable remainder.

limits.title: Deny-log scan padding per endpoint
limits.counting: Symmetric padding after flooring the runner client's start and ceiling its end to whole seconds. Allows for differences between the client's wall clock and the archive's displayed event timestamps; does not guarantee delivery or coverage under every clock condition.
limits.effect: Queries floor(start) - 2 seconds through ceil(end) + 2 seconds; records in either pad remain eligible for correlation. Raw client milliseconds are unchanged; reversed endpoints still prevent collection.
limits.control: Fixed; no public override. window.pad_seconds records the pad; absence in older envelopes means zero.
limits.behavior: Independent timestamp fixtures cover both padding regions, exact and exterior bounds, equal spans and rollback. Complete full, early-only, late-only and empty replies preserve eligible candidates and missing-record diagnostics through assembly, serialization and consumer recovery.

limits.title: Default log collection timeout
limits.counting: Shared CLOCK_MONOTONIC allowance starting before observer launch; includes startup, inner log show capture and processing. Standalone show uses the same finite default.
limits.effect: Expiry stops collection and starts the fixed cleanup grace; available diagnostics survive without associations.
limits.control: Override with --log-timeout-ms: positive integer milliseconds representable as a monotonic deadline plus cleanup grace. Validated before runner invocation even with --no-log-capture.
limits.behavior: Independent slow-success and permanent-hang fixtures prove that a larger finite allowance buys waiting time only; shared absolute deadlines are not restarted by the observer.

limits.title: Log cleanup grace
limits.counting: Cleanup ends no later than the original collection deadline plus this grace; early failures start the grace immediately.
limits.effect: Unconfirmed reaping or group absence is reported; retries never restart the allowance.
limits.behavior: Owned orphan controls cover leader death before reply, pipes open or closed, group absence, failed signalling/probing and lost ownership. The bound concerns supervised waiting, not OS scheduling.

limits.title: Parsed deny events
limits.counting: Parsed deny events in show output and the derived controller array.
limits.effect: An additional event makes capture incomplete and correlation unavailable; bounded raw output and available diagnostic events survive.
limits.behavior: Exact and over-limit fixtures retain diagnostics and distinguish complete capture from overflow.

limits.title: Candidate associations
limits.counting: Total event-to-step candidates, including ambiguous matches.
limits.effect: Excess discards the whole derived association result and withholds correlation; retained events remain diagnostic.
limits.behavior: A 256-record unique-path control preserves all associations; repeated matching attempts exhaust the candidate budget.

limits.title: Candidate allocation allowance
limits.counting: Conservative encoded/allocation charge per candidate: six times the sum of twice the step-ID length plus path, operation, kind and action lengths, plus 1,024 bytes of structure.
limits.effect: Excess discards all associations and withholds correlation.
limits.behavior: Long repeated paths exercise the allocation allowance independently of the candidate count. This is a derived-data bound, not a peak-process-memory claim.

limits.title: Steps admitted to correlation
limits.counting: Each of the submitted plan and returned step arrays.
limits.effect: Excess withholds log correlation; execution evidence is unchanged.
limits.behavior: A 256-step control preserves unique candidates; over-limit arrays reject correlation.

limits.title: Observer JSON structure
limits.counting: Opening object/array delimiters, commas and colons outside quoted strings, counted before allocating a JSON tree.
limits.effect: Excess retains bounded raw diagnostic text and withholds parsing and correlation.
limits.behavior: Independent oversized JSON array trips the structural guard before Value allocation.

limits.title: Observer echoed metadata
limits.counting: Each echoed show argument: predicate, process name, start, end, last, plan, row and correlation ID.
limits.effect: Observer rejects excess before launching log show; controller also rejects oversized reply metadata.
limits.behavior: Receiver malformed-shape controls cover excess metadata; direct argument admission is source-inspected.

limits.title: Policy helper output
limits.counting: Per stdout or stderr stream captured from sbpl-check. Byte prefix before lossy text decoding; independent of the runner reply budget.
limits.effect: Output beyond the prefix is marked truncated. Truncated JSON stdout is not parsed as a complete reply.
limits.behavior: The shared receiver accepts an explicit per-stream retention budget for this producer; exact byte counts, truncation and JSON parse suppression are tested independently of the runner budget.

limits.title: Rejected validator frame context
limits.counting: Raw prefix of the first rejected frame, before base64 encoding.
limits.effect: The remaining frame is not retained as context; frame_bytes, retained_bytes and context_truncated describe the loss.
limits.behavior: Exact and over-limit invalid-frame context controls; no rejected bytes become verdicts.

limits.title: Exec child output per stream
limits.counting: Retained bytes in each stdout/stderr text buffer, excluding NUL. A truncation marker occupies part of this space on overflow.
limits.effect: Additional output is drained but not retained.
limits.behavior: Small stdout/stderr capture is tested. Overflow truncation and the exact retained-prefix/marker split are source-inspected.

limits.title: Primary worker diagnostic
limits.counting: Diagnostic payload bytes, excluding NUL.
limits.effect: The primary diagnostic is bounded and reports retained length and truncation state; it is not a transcript.
limits.behavior: Bounded diagnostic/truncation controls in the Swift worker evidence tests.

limits.title: Optional compiled-object capture
limits.counting: Raw bytecode bytes for a nonempty supported single-profile (type 0) object, before base64 encoding.
limits.effect: Oversize or unsupported objects leave capture unavailable without preventing policy application.
limits.behavior: Independently constructed object controls cover exact, excessive and unsupported captures.

limits.title: Worker observed path
limits.counting: Per-step C path-buffer payload bytes, excluding NUL.
limits.effect: Path observation can be absent or bounded; a host-side path diagnostic is a separate observation.
limits.behavior: Source-inspected buffer use; no exact path-length behavior claim is tested.

limits.title: Worker attempt error text
limits.counting: Per-step error-buffer payload bytes, excluding NUL.
limits.effect: Error prose is bounded; structured result/status fields remain separate.
limits.behavior: Source-inspected bounded formatting; no exact error-text boundary claim is tested.

limits.title: sbpl-check source admission
limits.counting: Top-level source bytes read by the diagnostic helper; not the runner policy cap.
limits.effect: policy_too_large without a compile verdict.
limits.behavior: Oversized input is tested through the shipped helper and fallback CLI; exact boundary behavior is source-inspected.

limits.title: sbpl-check import inventory depth
limits.counting: Top-level imports start at depth 0. At depth 8 the helper records a depth-limit diagnostic instead of reading/expanding that file.
limits.effect: Stops inventory expansion on that branch and marks imports_truncated. Does not impose this depth on libsandbox compilation.
limits.behavior: Deep import-chain control in the helper unit tests.

limits.title: sbpl-check import inventory count
limits.counting: Maximum records accumulated by the helper traversal, including unresolved/error records; visited files/names are deduplicated.
limits.effect: Stops further inventory traversal and marks imports_truncated. Does not impose this count on libsandbox compilation.
limits.behavior: Import-count exhaustion control in the helper unit tests.

limits.title: Log observer stream text
limits.counting: Streaming helper mode only (--duration or --follow): retained nonempty, non-prelude log lines with one LF per line. Only whole lines that fit are retained.
limits.effect: The first overflowing line sets log_truncated and stops text accumulation. Deny-event arrays and JSONL emission continue separately; this is not a memory or total-report cap. The normal CLI log-show path does not use this inner cap.
limits.control: Fixed byte cap; --no-log-capture disables normal CLI log collection, not this helper capability.
limits.behavior: Compiled value agreement is tested. Streaming accumulation and overflow behavior are source-inspected.
